title: Ideal ADC LSB voltage
description: Find the ideal code-bin width for an N-bit converter from its full-scale input span.
assumptions: Uniform ideal converter with 2^N code bins covering the specified full-scale span.
Full-scale span is the upper reference minus the lower reference, not the voltage of the highest reconstruction level.
Resolution does not establish accuracy; offset, gain, INL, DNL and noise are excluded.

references.title: Texas Instruments SLAA694A, General Oversampling of MSP ADCs for Higher Resolution, section 2.1, equation 1

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.

title: Ideal ADC code and quantization error
description: Quantize a specific input voltage using an explicitly defined uniform midrise transfer, then report its midpoint reconstruction and signed error.
formula: q = (V_high - V_low)/2^N; k = floor((V_in - V_low)/q); V_hat = V_low + (k + 1/2)q; error = V_hat - V_in
assumptions: Uniform midrise model: bin k is [V_low+kq, V_low+(k+1)q), reconstructed at its midpoint.
The input is inside the nonsaturated interval V_low <= V_in < V_high; the upper endpoint is excluded.
Unsigned straight-binary code labels are used even when the analog interval is bipolar.
This explicit midpoint convention is not a universal device transfer curve; consult device transition specifications. Offset, INL, DNL, noise and saturation behavior are excluded.

references.title: University of Texas at Austin EE445S, Lecture 8 Quantization notes, midrise quantization and error analysis
Texas Instruments ADCPro User Guide SBAU128C, appendix A.1.1 ADC transfer and quantization error

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.
The upper endpoint must exceed the lower endpoint by at least 1 nV.
Input must not lie below the nonsaturated converter interval.
Input must remain below full scale after floating-point normalization.
Input must be below the excluded upper endpoint.

title: Bandlimited ideal quantization SNR
description: Estimate ideal sine-wave SNR after digital filtering to a specified noise bandwidth, including signal backoff and white-quantization-noise process gain.
formula: OSR = f_s/(2B); SNR_linear = a*2^N*sqrt((3/2)*OSR); SNR_dB = 20 log10(SNR_linear); process_gain_dB = 10 log10(OSR)
assumptions: Quantization error is approximately zero-mean white noise, uniformly distributed between -q/2 and +q/2, with total variance q^2/12.
The sine-wave peak-to-peak amplitude is a times the converter full-scale span and remains in the linear input range.
The sine lies within a unity-gain digital passband whose one-sided equivalent noise bandwidth is B; noise outside B is rejected.
The sine spans at least 16 LSBs as a conservative applicability screen; this does not guarantee uncorrelated error for coherent tones or undithered inputs.
No noise shaping, overload, harmonic distortion, thermal/reference noise, clock jitter or analog noise budget is modeled. Raising sample rate without filtering does not provide this process gain.

references.title: Texas Instruments SLAP082, Signal Acquisition and Conditioning Seminar section 2, slide 2-15: q/sqrt(12) and ideal sine SNR
Texas Instruments SLAA694A, General Oversampling of MSP ADCs for Higher Resolution, section 2.2 and equation 4

inputs.label: Sine peak-to-peak fraction of full scale

outputs.label: Signal RMS to in-band quantization RMS ratio

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.
Digital noise bandwidth must not exceed the Nyquist bandwidth.
The sine must span at least 16 LSBs for this quantization-noise approximation.

title: Dynamic ENOB from measured SINAD
description: Express a real converter's measured noise-plus-distortion performance as the bit resolution of an equivalent ideal full-scale sine converter.
assumptions: SINAD is an independently measured full-scale sine signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio, excluding DC and including harmonics and noise over the stated Nyquist measurement band.
Exact logarithmic constants are used rather than the rounded 6.02 and 1.76 constants.
No amplitude-backoff correction is applied; below-full-scale tests require normalization outside this calculation.

This is a dynamic figure of merit, not DC noise-free resolution, static accuracy, or a separation of noise from distortion. A narrowband or noise-shaped result is not directly comparable to this full-Nyquist convention.
ENOB is continuous and may be negative for very poor SINAD; do not clamp or round it to an integer.

references.title: Texas Instruments ADCPro User Guide SBAU128C, appendix A.1.3.5, equation 4: dynamic ENOB versus DC noise-based resolution
Texas Instruments SLAP082, Signal Acquisition and Conditioning Seminar section 2, slide 2-15

title: Baseband Nyquist sampling margin
description: Compare a selected sample rate against the highest frequency in a bandlimited baseband input and show the available anti-alias transition interval.
formula: f_N = f_s/2; margin = f_N - f_max; rate_ratio = f_s/(2f_max)
assumptions: Uniform real-valued baseband sampling; the highest input frequency is positive and includes all signal components that must be preserved.
Strict positive margin is needed for the stated no-alias baseband condition; zero margin is a boundary, not a safe practical design.
A negative margin intentionally reports an undersampled design and is not an invalid arithmetic input.
Practical anti-alias attenuation, out-of-band interferers, filter order, ADC aperture response and bandpass undersampling are not calculated.

references.title: Texas Instruments AN-236/SNAA079C, An Introduction to the Sampling Theorem, sections 2 and 4

outputs.label: Rate relative to twice highest frequency

title: Sampled tone alias frequency
description: Fold a nonnegative analog tone frequency into the first Nyquist zone of a real-valued sampled sequence.
formula: k = floor(f_in/f_s + 1/2); f_alias = abs(f_in - k f_s)
assumptions: A single tone is uniformly sampled at an exact fixed sample rate; real-valued first-zone alias magnitude is reported in [0, f_s/2].
Frequencies differing by an integer sample-rate multiple are indistinguishable; negative frequencies are reflected to their positive magnitudes.
No phase, spectral inversion direction, anti-alias attenuation or converter input bandwidth is modeled. A computed alias does not establish that the ADC can acquire the analog tone.
The input-to-sample-rate ratio is capped at 1e9 to limit loss of floating-point precision in subtracting large sample-rate multiples.

references.title: Texas Instruments AN-236/SNAA079C, An Introduction to the Sampling Theorem, spectrum replication and folding in sections 3 and 4

constraints.message: Input frequency must not exceed one billion times the sample rate for this numerical model.

title: Ideal unipolar DAC output voltage
description: Find the ideal static analog voltage commanded by an unsigned DAC code, including a configured reference-to-output gain.
formula: V_span = gain * V_ref; V_out = code * V_span/2^N; V_max_code = (2^N - 1)*V_span/2^N
assumptions: Straight-binary unipolar DAC; configured gain includes any reference division and output-buffer gain.
The denominator is 2^N, not 2^N-1; the highest code is one ideal LSB below the configured span.
The output amplifier has sufficient supply headroom and load capability; reference error, offset, INL, DNL, settling, glitches and output loading are excluded.
This generic transfer law is not a claim that every gain or reference value is supported by the cited DAC device.

references.title: Texas Instruments DAC80501/DAC70501/DAC60501 datasheet SBAS794E, section 8.3.1.1, equation 1

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.
DAC code must be an integer.
Code exceeds the selected DAC resolution.

title: SAR ADC half-LSB acquisition settling
description: Estimate acquisition time for the SAR sampling capacitor to settle an input step to half an N-bit LSB through source and sampling-switch resistance.
formula: tau = (R_source + R_switch) C_sample; alpha = abs(step)/V_span; t_min = tau ln(alpha * 2^(N+1))
assumptions: Single-pole switched-capacitor acquisition model; the input stays constant during acquisition and source/switch resistances are linear and time-invariant.
Step fraction is the magnitude of the initial capacitor-to-input voltage difference divided by full-scale span, with 0 < alpha <= 1.
The initial error must exceed half an LSB; already-settled inputs are outside this positive-time model.
Alpha = 1 represents a worst-case full-scale step; alpha = 1/2 represents a half-scale initial error, giving N ln(2) time constants.

Sampling capacitance and switch resistance must come from the selected ADC. Charge buckets, amplifier nonlinear settling, multiple poles, kickback, parasitics and tolerances are not modeled; add datasheet-based margin.
This is acquisition time only, not conversion time or maximum throughput, and it does not certify converter accuracy.

references.title: Texas Instruments SBAA081A, Using a SAR Analog-to-Digital Converter for Current Measurement in Motor Control Applications, section 5, equations 5-10

constraints.message: Resolution must be an integer number of bits.
Total acquisition resistance must be positive.
Initial error must exceed half an LSB for this positive acquisition-time model.
